title: Orientation comparison
description: Compare Earth reference coastlines with their mathematical rotation into Erde's selected spin frame.
reading: Earth-reference land geometry is rotated into the chosen Erde frame. This is an orientation scaffold; it does not calculate the effects of an alternate geological history on shorelines.

title: Latitude and climate potential
description: New-latitude forcing bands with reference sites; separates geometric constraints from unmodeled regional climates.
reading: The same land geometry is compared with new latitude bands. The bands represent solar-forcing potential, not a climate simulation or a finished biome map.

title: Relief and passages
description: An approximate mountain and passage scaffold for planning isolation, rain shadows, and migration.
reading: Approximate mountain and passage axes suggest where elevation and barriers could shape movement. Relief and routes are illustrative rather than surveyed.

title: Ancestry and dispersal
description: Locate the selected African ancestry, Sunda radiation, Sahul branch, and early American migration without inventing political borders.
reading: Ancestry and dispersal overlays connect the African stem, Sunda radiation, Sahul branch and early American migration. They are historical scenarios rather than exact tracks.

title: American contact landscape
description: Defined-epoch map of the five First American regional complexes and the northern successor outcome.
reading: The five First American regional complexes are shown at the atlas’s defined epoch. The northern successor outcome does not erase independent southern histories.

title: Day night and twilight ring
description: Orthographic views show that the terminator is a great circle, with the provisional habitable envelope around it.
reading: The star-facing and dark hemispheres meet along a great-circle terminator. The marked habitable envelope is provisional; the terminator itself is not a guaranteed biological boundary.

title: Climate and surface life
description: Global target-envelope map with thermal ranges and the distinction between photic habitat and a mostly dark fringe.
reading: The central dayside is hot, the deep nightside cold, and the twilight region intermediate. The lit habitat and the mostly dark fringe have different energy constraints.

title: Ecological provinces
description: A scaled hypothetical sector showing fragmented wet provinces, mountain passes, salt barriers, terminal brines, and large lakes.
reading: A hypothetical twilight sector contains wet provinces separated by rain shadows and salt basins. Passes and river valleys connect habitats; this is not a mapped continent.

title: Water circulation
description: A process map connecting river catchments and lakes to evaporation, precipitation, ice storage, and conditional slow return.
reading: Candidate transport mechanisms, not a solved water cycle. The reference inventory totals 240 million km³ water-equivalent. Basal melt, hydraulic head and sustainable return require coupled testing.

title: Mountain settlements and depth
description: A shared vertical datum makes mountain-city altitude distinct from rock cover and lowland mine depth.
reading: Mountain-city altitude is measured above surrounding terrain; rock cover is measured to the overlying surface. High-altitude rooms can have shallow cover, while lowland mines can be much deeper.

title: Dwarven habitat preferences
description: Ecological placement of five dwarf species and the deep-massif subspecies, with no invented territorial boundaries.
reading: Five native dwarf species and a deep-massif subspecies occupy overlapping ecological settings. The diagram specifies habitat tendencies, not ethnic territories or political borders.

title: City facilities and regional support
description: An illustrative site map of hydropower, agriculture, ventilation, transit, and waste flows supporting underground settlement.
reading: A local facility plan within a larger food-and-water region. The complete watershed and productive capture area extend beyond this sheet; symbol size does not establish capacity.

title: Lake and oasis habitats
description: Compare an oxygenated lake food web above anoxic depths with a chemically powered, isolated subglacial oasis.
reading: Large lake fauna require productive oxygenated water. Small oasis consumers are a selected ecology, not a universal length ceiling; both chemical donor and acceptor fluxes must suffice.
